instruction.text: What do the bolded statements mean in this context?

atoms.a: Kathy hurt her knee this morning. This is just what she needed before the marathon.
b: ++Kathy’s injury occurred at an inconvenient time.
Kathy is happy about the injury.
Kathy will partake in the marathon.

feedback.end: This statement reflects sarcasm. The given situation is unfavourable, and the sarcastic comment underlines the gravity of the situation.

atoms.a: After a snow storm, Hope and her family can’t even open the door to their house. Hope states, “It looks like we got a bit of snow.”
b: ++ There was a lot of snowfall.
More snow is to be expected.

feedback.end: This statement is an understatement since there is more than a bit of snow. Understatements display less intensity than is expected in a situation.

atoms.a: Farina’s partner is snoring extremely loudly. She thinks to herself, “I’m going to rip my ears out one of these days.”
b: ++ Farina is irritated by the amount of noise her partner is making.
Farina thinks that ripping her ears out will reduce the noise.
Farina is not bothered by the noise at all.

feedback.end: This statement is an overstatement. The content of the sentence is overly exaggerated, since Farina does not literally want to rip her ears out. Like hyperboles, usage of overstatements allows the situation to appear more dramatic or extreme.

hint.text: Sarcasm, understatements and overstatements are all instances of verbal irony. Verbal irony is a figure of speech in which someone says one thing, but actually means something different.

instruction.text: What type of verbal irony does the following sentence include? Select the correct answer.

atoms.a: “My trip couldn’t be going better,” she mumbled to herself after realising she would have to wait 10 hours for her next connection.
After one hour of a heated discussion between Lukas and Miranda, Miranda stormed out of the room. Lukas looked at me and stated, “Hm, we have our differences.”
I’ll never forgive you if you forget to buy the chips.

instruction.text: Match the subcategories of verbal irony to their definitions.

atoms.b: the use of words that mean the opposite of what the speaker really thinks
purposefully not fully expressing the intensity of a situation
